title: Expanding the supply of euro safe assets
summary: ECB Executive Board Member Philip Lane delivered a keynote speech on 22 April 2026 arguing that the euro area suffers from an structural undersupply of euro-denominated safe assets, with Bunds being the primary but insufficient benchmark asset. Lane outlined various mechanisms for expanding the common bond supply, including the Blanchard-Ubide blue/red bond proposal, and noted that recent reforms have reduced inter-country sovereign spread volatility.
key_points: The current stock of Bunds is too small relative to the size of the euro area or the global financial system to meet demand for euro-denominated safe assets
Common factors now drive euro area bond markets with much less volatility in inter-country spreads, reflecting reforms including ESM backstops, NGEU, SSM, SRM, and ECB tools (TPI, OMT)
EUREP repo facility revisions make euro-denominated assets more attractive to global investors by enabling non-euro area central banks to address euro liquidity shortages
EU-level bonds (SURE, NGEU) are priced similarly to GDP-weighted sovereign averages but are less liquid than French or German bonds
The speech references the Blanchard-Ubide 'blue bond/red bond' reform: ring-fencing national indirect tax revenues to back commonly issued bonds, creating larger common bond stock
Common bonds could expand through joint financing of European public goods (defence, Ukraine funding) matched with shared fiscal capacity
Lane cites work by Hildebrand, Rey, and Schularick on principles for expanding shared defence capabilities and their common financing framework
why_it_matters: Safe assets are foundational infrastructure for financial markets—used as benchmarks for pricing, collateral in repo/derivatives markets, and hedges during stress. A structural undersupply of euro safe assets affects everything from sovereign spreads to repo market functioning to the euro's international role. Lane's speech signals ECB concern about this structural gap and willingness to consider policy mechanisms (blue/red bonds, expanded EUREP) to address it.
market_structure_context: Core speech topic is euro area safe asset architecture. Addresses: (1) safe asset definition (liquid, hedge in stress), (2) undersupply problem and Bunds' dominant role, (3) liquidity comparison across sovereigns and EU bonds using bid-ask spreads, (4) EUREP repo facility mechanics and global backstop role, (5) blue/red bond proposal mechanics for expanding common bond stock, (6) trade-off between blue bond stock size and ring-fenced revenue requirements, (7) fixed-cost investment needed to build ancillary derivatives and repo markets.
